quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Your tire goes flat while you are riding. What should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake using the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake using the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold both handlebars firmly. Ease off the throttle and go straight. If you must brake, slowly use the brake on the good tire. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn by moving only your head and eyes. Press your knees against the gas tank to help balance the motorcycle. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medicines usually affect your body?

options.text: They make it hard to focus.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make you sleepy.
questions.explanation: Most medicines for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, or anxiety can make you sleepy and affect your ability to ride safely. Before riding, learn how any medicine you take affects your body.

questions.question: A driver is tailgating you. What should you do?

options.text: Move to one side of your lane to let them share it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up will only increase danger by making them tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles do.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: You cannot avoid an object or uneven surface. What should you do?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Rise off the seat slightly so your legs can absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise off the seat slightly so your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle or uneven surface, approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Slow down as much as you can. Keep the motorcycle upright and rise slightly off the seat so your knees can absorb some of the impact. Just before hitting it, roll on the throttle slightly to lift the front wheel.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:
questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with little experience.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have been riding for less than six months. Most crashes happen in daylight when riders are going at low speeds.

questions.question: Why should you use both the front and rear brakes every time you slow or stop?

options.text: Using only one brake will wear them unevenly.
It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
It is the only way to slow down a motorcycle.
The brakes only work when both are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes during normal stops helps you form the habit of always using both brakes. This habit will help you in emergencies, where using both brakes may be critical.

questions.question: In group riding, what does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Hand signals are important for communication when riding in groups. When the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with their palm facing back, all riders in the group should stop.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Keep your hands over the clutch and brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands over the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, school zones, and construction zones, keep your hands over the clutch and both brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can your body eliminate per hour?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. The time it takes to lower your blood alcohol content (BAC) varies. It is safest not to ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: How should your following distance at night compare to your following distance during the day?

options.text: You should allow a longer following distance at night.
You should allow a shorter following distance at night.
You should maintain the same following distance all day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should allow a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distance because you cannot see shadows or light contrasts clearly. Use a longer following distance at night than during the day.

questions.question: For routine braking, what should you do?

options.text: Alternate between front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Use both front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When someone follows you too closely, what should you do?

options.text: Do not worry and focus on the road ahead.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will make them tailgate at a higher speed, which is more dangerous. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers will not expect you there and may suddenly leave the road.

questions.question: What happens when your rear tire skids?

options.text: It is only a problem if the front tire is also skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a serious crash or death. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel. When the wheel locks, you lose the ability to steer. You must release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider stop other drivers from sharing the lane?

options.text: By giving dirty looks to other drivers
By riding in the center of the lane
By riding in the left side of the lane
By riding in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to close any large spaces on either side of your motorcycle. This makes it harder for drivers to try to share the lane with you.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for your friend.
Involve your friend in activities to slow their drinking.
Keep your friend from leaving until they are sober.
Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: There are several ways to prevent someone from riding while impaired. Arrange another way for them to get home, keep them busy with other activities, use any excuse to stop them from leaving before they are sober, and ask other friends to help intervene.

questions.question: How should a group of riders pass another vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider should not pass until the first rider has safely returned to the original lane. Riders should continue this pattern until all have safely passed.

questions.question: When riding near stopped or slow cars, what should a rider do?

options.text: Pull over and wait for traffic to move.
Ride on the shoulder to pass quickly.
Weave between cars to pass quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not weave between cars.
questions.explanation: Weaving between slow or parked cars puts you at risk from opening doors or cars pulling into traffic. If something unexpected happens, you will not have room to escape safely. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers will not expect you there.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used when you need to stop quickly.
Should be used only on slippery surfaces.
Is not as strong as the rear brake.
Is safe to use when used correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use when used correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes any time you slow down or stop. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It is safe to use if you use it properly.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Apply the brakes harder than normal.
Apply the brakes more gently than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes more gently than normal.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use caution. Apply the brakes more gently than you normally would.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders who wear helmets.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders who wear helmets, no matter what speed you are riding.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters. These signs tell you the rules of the road. You must follow them.
